verdict.rationale: Raygun documents its own source-map support: it fetches public maps automatically, accepts manual uploads via the JS source map center or its API (authenticated with an external access token), and uses the maps to turn minified errors into readable traces with source snippets. The API route is scriptable from CI, but the evidence never mentions a dedicated CLI or bundler plugin, which is the delivery path the story names. Missing for 10: a documented upload CLI or bundler plugin (webpack/Vite etc.), CI-specific upload docs, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can upload JavaScript source maps from CI — via CLI or bundler plugin — so production stack traces show my original source, not minified frames

citations.quote: you can also manually upload source maps either through our website using the `JS source map center` or via our API
Raygun uses them to take un-readable errors generated from minified JavaScript and translate them to be readable and to include code snippets from your source.
Uploading JavaScript files directly to Raygun
If your source maps are publicly available on your website Raygun will fetch them automatically without you having to do anything.
